shapes.text: Ling 285Human Language and TechnologyLecture 10Neural Networks 1.5

Khalil Iskarous
Department of Linguistics
University of Southern California
First Exam Next ThursdayPease bring a Pencil!

Imagine you are given many pictures of faces (48 Million pixels), and you’re asked to identify one of 1000 possible people. 
Imagine you are given speech waves and you’re asked to to identify for each, which of 25 sounds each speech wave corresponds to.
What can do this? A Neural Network (NN)
I will not tell you now why it’s called a NN. I will teach you what it is by what it does– how it walks and how it swims.
The job of an NN is to take a bunch of numbers the 48M pixels in one image/numbers of a wave and to return a probability distribution.
For speech the probability distribution is 25 sounds
But let’s say it had just 5 vowels, this is a pdf: [.2,.2,.4,.2,0]
And let’s say we agree the vowel order is read, rad, rude, Rud, rod
The p’s must sum to 1 (100%)
That says: there’s 20% chance the sound is the v in read, 20% it’s the vowel in rad, 40% the vowel in rude, 20% it’s the vowel in Rud, and 0% it’s the vowel in Rod.

The input of an NN is a bunch of numbers, signal, or a vector, e.g., [4,1,-3,2,1,.4,1,2,-3,…] (usually 1000’s of nums). Let’s say these are the pressure numbers of a speech wave
The output of the NN is a decision pdf: Given the signal, what’s the p(each object): p of each vowels read, rad, rude, Rud, rod 
How? How can NNs do that? How can it make a decision.
They have knowledge, in a bunch of weights w’s
And somehow the input signal vector is combined with these w’s and a decision about the object detected is made, eventually, as there are many many w’s and many many calculations! Several trillion w’s and billions of calculations.
These magical w’s allow the NN to make decisions, but how does it know these w’s???
Fake it till you make it!
SGD for NNs. You start out with random w’s.
Give it a signal (let’s say we give it the vowel in Rud)
Forward Propagation: It uses its stupid w’s, and it produces a pdf that doesn’t reflect reality: [.4,.1,.2,.2,.1]
We tell it: NO!!!!!!! You should have decided: 0,0,0,1,0], so it realizes it made a big Error or Loss
It improves its w’s to reduce the Loss
Give it another signal and repeat billions of times!
But what calculations are actullay made on the signal???

Learning: How does an NN learn the w’s? Specifically
Inference: How does an NN combine w’s with inputs? Specifically
We will answer question 2 first, since 2 is part of 1!!!
Santiago Ramón y Cajal, Recuerdos de mi vida, vol. II (1917), fig. 40. Cropped and rotated.
One neuron computes a weighted sum
Cajal: Brain is made of neurons
Inner Product, Scalar Product, Dot Product, ∫f*g

Cajal source: Santiago Ramón y Cajal, Recuerdos de mi vida, vol. II: Historia de mi labor científica (1917), Figure 40. https://www.gutenberg.org/files/60675/60675-h/60675-h.htm . Original image: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/60675/60675-h/images/ill_248fig40.jpg . The peripheral half is cropped and rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise so the main direction of flow is rightward. Circles mark the visible neuronal somata. The gold packets and selected contacts are schematic teaching overlays, not a claim about measured activity or a full anatomical reconstruction. Signed numerical activations are artificial-neuron quantities, not negative firing rates.

The three-input example is an artificial circuit: weights [-2,3,1], activations [-1,1,3], weighted sum 8, no bias.

1. Circles appear over the somata
2. Positive and negative activations glimmer
3. Arrows identify selected synaptic contacts
4. Signals travel rightward through the contacts
5. Arrows become synaptic w labels
6. w labels become signed weights
7. Only three inputs and one receiving neuron remain
8. Three edges carry weights −2, 3, 1
9. Input activations are −1, 1, 3
10. The inner product appears in the receiving neuron

Most engineers/neuroscientists/people: Modern AI has nothing to do with how humans  think, perceive, act, decide, etc. The brain is full of chemistry and electrical activity and abstract stuff, and that obviously is not part of LLMs, which are full of numbers and arithmetic!



A few people, including me: Modern AI is a set of evolutionary tinkerings for 100 years with how arithmetic can emulate brain chemical and electrical activity… And these attempts seem to have succeeded.

shapes.text: First Exam Next ThursdayPease bring a Pencil!

Learning FITYMI: Pick random w’s, and randomly pick I/O to  
learn from x = -2,1,3,-4,2 input and output 0,0,0,0,0,1,0

WRONG!!!!!! The actual pdf at the output should be 0,0,0,0,0,1,0. Change w’s to make the output pdf closer to the true one!!~!! Using SGD, now called Backpropagation!

And repeat this over and over again with billions of I/O pairs! That’s what’s done at data centers 

We want to estimate w, the average of [73,90,98,46,400,81,82,78,62,91,61,84,75,84,81,75]
Note that one of the numbers by mistake is 400 … the actual average of the list is about 100
But in reality, the datapoint 400 is a mistake, and the true average of the list, without that mistake is about 80!
